page: Google Cloud Platform m3-megamem-64 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the m3 instance family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.6 GHz, with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 976.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.25 GB per core. It contains no local storage and no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 60403.41 and a Passmark CPU score of 55058.84, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-core performance is average, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1577.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, reaching 151.0 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. Database operations are strong, scoring 26171.33 on Passmark, while Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 55.2 million operations per second.

The server represents a high resource density profile, prioritizing massive memory capacity over local storage and GPU acceleration. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring large memory footprints without the overhead of local NVMe drives. However, the lack of local storage means all data persistence must rely on network-attached storage, and the average single-core CPU performance may limit workloads bound by single-threaded execution.

This configuration is suited for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-intensive enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks such as software compilation, which scored 42621.0 in Geekbench tests. It also supports moderate LLM inference tasks, demonstrating a prompt processing speed of 2427.41 tokens per second for small models.
